extractor.prompt: Extract founding relations in Husserl's Thing and Space (1907), focusing on how higher-order perceptual and scientific objectivities are founded on lower strata of immediate experience.
extractor.note: Partial extraction covering Introduction and Section I (Chapters 1-2, ¶¶1-6) on foundational structure of perception and layered constitution. Focuses on how lower levels (perception, appearance-stratum) ground higher levels (scientific reality, doxic acts), the distinction between real and intentional content, and kinaesthetic motivation. Not covered: kinetic and kinaesthetic analyses (§§26-57), spatial constitution (Sections V-VI), higher theoretical cognition.

coverage_note: Covers Introduction (¶¶1-48) establishing foundational program, and foundational sections (¶¶49-190) on how perception as appearance-stratum grounds doxic position-takings and how perceptual manifolds are constituted through kinaesthetic motivation. Focused on the doctrine of layered constitution where each stratum presupposes and is built upon lower strata.

units.claim: Phenomenology of straightforward perceptual experience provides the necessary foundation for higher constitutive problems of scientific reality, not merely a preliminary exercise.
units.quote: the foundation without which the higher constitutive problems cannot even be posed

units.term: Layered constitution (higher strata building on lower)
units.claim: Higher constitutive strata of perceptual and scientific experience asymmetrically presuppose and are built upon lower strata of immediate sensory experience.
units.quote: the higher constitutive strata presuppose and build upon the lower, so that clarity about perception is a necessary condition for any future phenomenology of scientific cognition

units.claim: Investigation proceeds from the lowest stratum of perceptual constitution, which provides the foundation upon which all higher theoretically mediated cognition must build.
units.quote: The lectures will address only the lowest stratum of experiential givenness — perceptual constitution prior to all deduction, induction, and higher theoretical cognition

units.claim: Presence in the flesh is the foundational phenomenological characteristic that distinguishes perception from all other modes of consciousness and grounds all subsequent constitutional analysis.
units.quote: §4 provides the foundational concept of the entire lectures: presence in the flesh

units.term: Appearance-stratum as foundation of doxic stratum
units.claim: The appearance-stratum (pure presence-in-the-flesh) is the constant, foundational element underlying all doxic variations (belief, doubt, disbelief), which form a higher stratum built upon it.
units.quote: presence in the flesh is the *constant* element across all the doxic variations

units.claim: The distinction between real content genuinely belonging to perception and intentional content belonging to the object as presented grounds the entire analysis of thing-constitution.
units.quote: the conceptual axis around which the entire subsequent analysis of thing-constitution will turn
